claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a hierarchical heterostructure with multilevel chemical fluctuations and spatially varying microstructural motifs.
An integrated multiscale ML framework can directly link microstructural features of HfNbTiVAl10 to Young’s modulus, yield strength, and toughness.
The proposed framework can overcome current computational inefficiencies and prediction inaccuracies.
The surrogate would be trained on validated molecular-dynamics and phase-field simulation databases combined with limited high-fidelity experimental data.
Grain-boundary networks, phase distributions, and local chemical-fluctuation metrics can serve as physics-informed descriptors for predicting tensile and fracture properties.
Grain-size distributions, phase-connectivity maps, and chemical-fluctuation statistics capture local stress concentrations.
These microstructural descriptors capture barriers to dislocation motion and crack propagation.
Embedding microstructural physics in the ML model bypasses expensive iterative first-principles and CALPHAD simulations.
Pattern recognition and data-driven interpolation can map hierarchical microstructural features to macroscopic elastic modulus, yield strength, and fracture toughness.
The proposed framework will be approximately 10 times faster than full-scale multiscale simulations.
The proposed framework will reduce prediction error by roughly 20% relative to conventional DFT/CALPHAD or empirical-calibration methods.
Conventional high-throughput DFT, CALPHAD, and direct experimental-calibration approaches are computationally intensive.
Conventional approaches have limited predictive reliability for fracture toughness.
The method is reliable only when the sample microstructure lies within the model’s training domain.
Severe processing anomalies, scale-up effects, or unexpected toughening or softening mechanisms can make the model unreliable.
The estimated accuracy and efficiency gains are based on analogous ML advances in other complex alloys.
The model’s ability to capture extreme local inhomogeneities has not been established.
A blinded prospective benchmark with at least 10 independently processed samples can test predictions of Young’s modulus, yield strength, fracture toughness, and computational efficiency.
